extracted.intended_audience: International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) examiners, USPTO examiners acting as IPEA, and patent applicants/agents responding to Chapter II proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing PCT Chapter II (international preliminary) examination, preparing the International Preliminary Examination Report (PCT/IPEA/409), handling replies and amendments, and making novelty/inventive-step/industrial-applicability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date for prior art (PCT Rule 64.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the 'relevant date' for considering prior art for international preliminary examination as set out in PCT Rule 64.1(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (i) generally the international filing date of the international application under international preliminary examination (subject to (ii) and (iii)); (ii) if the application claims priority and the international filing date is within the priority period, the filing date of the earlier application (unless the IPEA considers the priority claim invalid); (iii) if the international filing date is later than the expiry of the priority period but within two months of that date and the application claims priority of an earlier application, the filing date of the earlier application (unless the IPEA considers the priority claim invalid for reasons other than the late filing). Parallel subparagraphs (B) and (C) reiterate these points. Examiners must apply these provisions when determining the relevant date for novelty and inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of claimed priority date validity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a document was published between a claimed priority date and the international filing date, the examiner must decide whether the claimed priority date is valid for determining the relevant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications filed on/after April 1, 2007, a priority date should not be considered invalid merely because the international application was filed within two months after the priority period expired. If there is insufficient time for the examiner to make a proper determination (e.g., need to issue a timely written opinion), the relevant date for the written opinion will be based on the claimed priority date. See WIPO Chapter 11 guidance. If the priority claim cannot be decided timely, treat the claimed priority date as the relevant date for the written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of documents published after relevant date but with earlier filing or priority dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Published applications or patents that were published on/after the relevant date but were filed earlier than the relevant date or claim priority to an earlier application filed before the relevant date are not considered part of the prior art for novelty and inventive step purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not considered prior art for novelty/inventive step, such documents must still be listed on the international preliminary examination report (Form PCT/ISA/237, PCT/IPEA/408, or PCT/IPEA/409) under the heading 'CERTAIN PUBLISHED DOCUMENTS'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-acknowledged prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art acknowledged by the applicant in the description should be regarded as correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such acknowledged prior art should be used during preliminary examination where appropriate and may be taken into account in determining inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling oral or non-written disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral or other non-written disclosures must be handled according to the PCT Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PCT Rules 64.2 and 70.9 for guidance on oral/non-written disclosures and how they affect novelty/inventive-step/industrial-applicability assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty assessment (PCT Article 33(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention is considered novel if it is not anticipated by the prior art as defined in the Regulations (PCT Article 33(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition applies for international preliminary examination and mutatis mutandis to the ISA written opinion (see PCT Rule 43 bis.1(b)). Explanations in the report should clearly point to the criterion of novelty where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness) assessment (PCT Article 33(3) and Rule 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention involves an inventive step if, with regard to the prior art as defined, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art at the prescribed relevant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT Rule 65.1 requires considering each claim's relation to the prior art as a whole, including combinations of documents or parts where such combinations would be obvious to a person skilled in the art. PCT Rule 65.2 confirms the relevant date for inventive step is Rule 64.1. The examiner should consider combinations and the overall teaching of the prior art when assessing inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability assessment (PCT Article 33(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention is industrially applicable if, according to its nature, it can be made or used in any kind of industry (broad sense, as in Paris Convention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is applied for the international preliminary examination and in the written opinion. Explanations in the report should indicate whether the criterion of industrial applicability is met for each claim examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted replies to the written opinion (Article 34; Rule 66)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may respond to the written opinion by making amendments and/or submitting arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be submitted directly to the IPEA (Rule 66.3(b)). Amendments, arguments, and rectifications of obvious mistakes received after the Authority has begun to draw up the written opinion or report need not be taken into account (Rule 66.4 bis). Applicants are strongly encouraged to file amendments promptly; no extensions of time for reply are permitted under 37 CFR 1.484(d). If no timely reply is received, the IPEA will prepare the report treating each claim substantially as in the written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'amendment' (Rule 66.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change other than rectification of an obvious mistake in claims, description, or drawings (including cancellation of claims or omission of passages/drawings) is an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are governed by PCT Rule 66.5 and must follow the form requirements of Rule 66.8. The IPEA/US will not accept non-English applications or amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for amendments (Rule 66.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending the description or drawings, replacement sheets must be submitted for every sheet that differs, accompanied by a letter drawing attention to differences and indicating the basis for the amendment in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment is deletion or minor alteration/addition, a copy of the relevant sheet containing alterations may be used provided clarity and reproducibility are not adversely affected. If an entire sheet is cancelled, a letter cancelling the sheet must be submitted. Replacement sheets should be typed clean copies without underlining/bracketing; a marked-up copy may be included as part of remarks. Any paper not in letter form must be accompanied by a signed letter (PCT Rule 92.1) drawing attention to differences between replaced and replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment format and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending claims in reply to a written opinion, a replacement sheet or sheets containing a complete set of claims must be submitted replacing all previously filed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The replacement claims must comply with Rule 46.5 mutatis mutandis and be accompanied by a letter that (i) identifies claims differing from originally filed claims and draws attention to differences, (ii) identifies originally filed claims cancelled by the amendments, and (iii) indicates the basis for the amendments in the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter — examiner's obligation and consequences (PCT Article 34(2)(b); Rule 70.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must ensure amendments filed do not go beyond the disclosure of the international application as filed; amendments introducing new matter must be disregarded for establishing the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is introduced, the international preliminary examination report will be established as if the amendment had not been made and must indicate reasons why the amendment goes beyond the disclosure (Rule 70.2(c)). Even where new matter on a replacement sheet is disregarded, other parts of the same replacement sheet that do not constitute new matter will be taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews — entitlement, conduct, and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview (telephone or personal) may be requested after filing a demand and during the reply time limit; only one interview is a matter of right, additional interviews are discretionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All substantive interviews must be made of record using PCT/IPEA/428 Notice on Informal Communication with the Applicant. When arranging an interview, the matters for discussion should be stated. Records should indicate whether a reply is due from the applicant or whether the examiner plans to issue an additional written opinion or establish the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and deadlines for replies and amendments; no extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to the written opinion must be filed within the set reply time limit to assure consideration; extensions are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.484(d) does not allow extensions of time for reply. Amendments filed at or before expiration of the reply period will be considered; amendments filed after may not be considered since examiners draw up reports promptly. However, if the report is not yet completed and it is apparent a late-filed response would result in a favorable report, the examiner may take it into account. Applicants are strongly encouraged to file amendments promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form of the International Preliminary Examination Report (PCT Article 35 and Admin Instructions Section 604)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must be established within prescribed time and form and must not state whether the claimed invention is patentable under national law; for each examined claim it should state whether the claim appears to satisfy novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability, with citations and explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations must clearly point to which of the three criteria any cited document is applicable and describe with reference to cited documents the reasons supporting conclusions. Explanations should be concise and preferably short sentences. If Article 34(4)(a) situations exist, the report must state that opinion and reasons and not contain the paragraph (2) statements. The report is established on Form PCT/IPEA/409.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for establishing the Chapter II report (PCT Rule 69.2 / Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA must establish the international preliminary examination report within the prescribed time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must be established within: (A) 28 months from the priority date; or (B) 6 months from the time provided under PCT Rule 69.1 for the start of international preliminary examination; or (C) 6 months from date of receipt by IPEA of the translation furnished under Rule 55.2, whichever expires last. Office practice completes internal processing by 27 months to meet 28-month target so applicants have time before national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up search requirement and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing the Chapter II report, the IPEA should conduct a top-up search to identify prior art that became available after the international search report and that could affect examination (intermediate prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A top-up search is distinct from an 'additional search' and is intended to find recently available prior art (e.g., applications published on/after the filing or valid priority date but with earlier filing/priority dates). Top-up searches should be performed in all Chapter II examinations except in rare circumstances (e.g., subject matter not examinable, application so unclear no meaningful opinion can be formed, or no international search for certain claims). When lack of unity applies to only part of claimed subject matter, the top-up search should be restricted to parts subject to Chapter II examination. If International Search Report documents already show novelty-destroying references and no amendments/comments were filed, a top-up search may serve no useful purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up search handling when lack of unity or unclear basis for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims lack unity, or an Article 34 amendment has no locatable basis or no explanatory letter was filed, the scope of the top-up search is limited accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims lack unity, examiner issues invitation to pay further fees and performs top-up search only on inventions for which fees were paid. If Article 34 amendment has no basis, the top-up search may be limited to the scope of claims forming the basis for the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuing a second written opinion when new objections arise from top-up search
rubrics_metrics.description: If the top-up search discovers relevant documents and the examiner intends to raise a new objection based on them, a second written opinion should be issued when the new objection was not necessitated by an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the applicant has notice and an opportunity to reply to new issues identified after the initial written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and annexing of amendments in the report
rubrics_metrics.description: The international preliminary examination report must identify the basis on which it is established (which amendments were taken into account) and attach replacement sheets taken into account as annexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets containing amendments under Articles 19 and/or 34 that have been taken into account are attached as annexes. Amendments under Article 19 reversed by Article 34 are not annexed. Superseded amendments are normally not included; but if a second replacement sheet for the same numbered sheet goes beyond the original disclosure, both first and second replacement sheets shall be attached and marked per PCT Administrative Instructions Section 602.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PCT/IPEA/409 completion guidance — Box I (Basis of report and amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for completing Box No. I (itemizing basis of report, listing substitute sheets, sequence listing information, and indicating amendments going beyond original disclosure or rectifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must indicate whether report is based on the international application in the language filed or on translations/amendments; list substitute/rectified/incorporated-by-reference sheets as originally filed where appropriate; indicate if any amendments resulted in cancellation of pages/claims/sheets/figures/sequence listing; point out in item 4 any amendments considered to go beyond original disclosure and explain determination (new matter disregarded for report but other non-new-matter amendments considered); mark item 5 if report takes into account rectification of obvious mistake (Rule 91); mark item 6 whether top-up searches were carried out and provide dates and whether additional relevant documents were discovered (documents used to support negative statements cited in Box V; certain documents cited in Box VI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PCT/IPEA/409 completion guidance — Box II (Priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box II is used to inform the applicant if the report is established as if the priority claim had not been made and to state reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report may be established as if priority not made where: (A) IPEA requested but was not furnished a copy of the earlier application (PCT Rule 66.7(a)); (B) applicant failed to timely comply with an invitation to furnish a translation of the earlier application (Rule 66.7(b)); (C) priority claim found invalid or all claims directed to inventions not described/enabled by earlier application (Rule 64.1). If only certain claims are affected, specify which claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PCT/IPEA/409 completion guidance — Box III (Non-establishment of opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box III indicates when a reasoned opinion on novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability has not been established for some or all claims and requires specification of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must specify that the report was not established because: (A) subject matter does not require international preliminary examination; (B) description, claims or drawings so unclear that no meaningful opinion could be formed; (C) claims are so inadequately supported by the description that no meaningful opinion could be formed; (D) no international search report has been established for the claims; (E) examiner concluded the application did not comply with unity of invention but decided not to issue an invitation to restrict claims or pay additional fees. If examining less than all claims, indicate which parts were/were not the subject of examination. If lack of meaningful opinion stems from sequence listing non-compliance with WIPO ST.26 or late furnishing fee unpaid, indicate reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PCT/IPEA/409 completion guidance — Box IV (Lack of unity of invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box IV is used to indicate results of unity of invention matters, including whether claims were restricted or additional fees were paid (with or without protest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether: (A) claims have been restricted; (B) additional fees paid without protest; (C) additional fees paid by the applicant under protest; (D) priority claim withdrawn. If additional fees paid under protest, the text of the protest and decision must be annexed to the report if applicant requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PCT/IPEA/409 completion guidance — Box V (Reasoned statement and citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box V contains the reasoned statement under Article 35(2) regarding novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability and the citations/explanations supporting those statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should state, in relation to each examined claim, whether the claim appears to satisfy the criteria and should cite documents believed to support the conclusions with concise explanations pointing to the criteria to which cited documents are applicable and reasons for the IPEA's conclusions.
